title: harness: oracle subset comparison rounds away wrong wide-integer results
description:
The independent expectation judge treats different integer results as equal by converting every numeric value to binary64 (harness/lib/compare.py:194).
compare.judge({'exit':0,'stdout_json':{'payload':9007199254740992}}, 0, b'{"payload":9007199254740993}', '') returns [] (no error), although the payload differs by one bit. compare_json correctly reports one hard difference for the same values. This path is used by corpora.isa_vectors for stdout_json expectations and engine.Runner._judge; if both executors have the same wrong wide-integer result, pairwise agreement cannot recover the lost oracle check.
Repro: timeout 45s python3 /home/tobias/Projects/bennett-workspace/bennett-conformance/.tmp/rev-conformance/repro_gate.py against frozen reviewed head 847f851cc5610ddf0edc5435c513a4ef87c6c5fc prints 'wrong wide-integer oracle judgment: []'. Preserve exact integer comparison and keep deliberate float behavior separate. No current published vector above 2^53 was found; the judging API path itself is reachable and the bad judgment was reproduced.
close_reason: Compare numeric values without float coercion: exact wide integers and mixed int/float comparisons; preserve float value and boolean behavior. Red regression reproduced adjacent integers and shared executor error; also reproduced integer-to-float overflow. Verified: cd /home/tobias/Projects/bennett-workspace/bennett-conformance/harness/tests && timeout 120s python3 -m unittest -v test_compare test_engine test_corpora (48 tests passed). title: checker: sampled tables are checked against drawn elements instead of the declared domain
description:
The sampled-table validator rejects valid complete tables and accepts missing rows (checker/src/eval.rs:3220-3255).
ISA 0.9 §12.1 'Table tuples' requires rows in domain order, one per distinct declared domain element including sampled claims; duplicate/missing rows reject. For identity perm_action @a (t:wire mut) () () () (), domain t=0..1, invocation args=[], budget=[0,0,0,0], sampler xoshiro256** seed=[1,0,0,0], count=1, the draw is t=0. The valid two-row identity table rejects ('table has 2 rows; sampling drew 1 distinct elements'); truncating it to row t=0 returns overall=verified, claim=evidence, coverage=1/2.
Repro: timeout 120s cargo run --manifest-path /home/tobias/Projects/bennett-workspace/bennett-conformance/.tmp/rev-conformance/repro/Cargo.toml -j4 --quiet at reviewed head 847f851cc5610ddf0edc5435c513a4ef87c6c5fc, cases sampled_full_table and sampled_missing_row. Validate the table over the declared domain, then use the drawn subset for execution and coverage.

title: rung 4: NaN amplitudes pass the state comparison with zero error
description:
The rung-4 amplitude acceptance check silently accepts invalid state amplitudes (ladder/rung-4/gate.py:149; JSON ingestion at :636).

title: checker: qif branches skip unconditional lifetimes and reject valid cross-arm allocation
description:
Basis replay selects only one qif arm (checker/src/eval.rs:1559-1567), whereas ISA 0.9 §§3.5, 4.6, 5.3 execute both arms' unconditional lifetimes with controlled gates, explicitly allowing lifetimes across arms.
Source action @a (t:wire mut) (c:wire in) () () (); ^entry(): qif c { d = qalloc any 1 } { qfree d } is the identity on all four (t,c) inputs: allocation and clean release are unconditional. For c=1, the checker skips qfree and rejects its correct identity table with E_CERT_REPLAY 'leaves allocations live at exit'. The source has matching allocation/release and needs no arm-local lifetime restriction.
Repro: timeout 120s cargo run --manifest-path /home/tobias/Projects/bennett-workspace/bennett-conformance/.tmp/rev-conformance/repro/Cargo.toml -j4 --quiet, case qif_lifetimes, at reviewed head 847f851cc5610ddf0edc5435c513a4ef87c6c5fc. timeout 45s python3 /home/tobias/Projects/bennett-workspace/bennett-conformance/.tmp/rev-conformance/repro_gate.py independently proves the same identity table. Give qif its full predicated expansion, including unconditional allocation and cleanup; do not narrow valid source programs to arm-local lifetimes.

title: Rung-4 estimate: use ideal-all-to-all target and full N=2^20 launch; adapter accepts bound pins (from bennett-estimate)
description:
Source: bennett-estimate/.tmp/sol-estimate/cross-repo-beads.md, "Consumer follow-up for bennett-conformance: rung-4 estimate inputs and capacity" (queued consumer fix; not a restriction of the full rung and not a request to adopt an unpublished ISA policy).

Determination: the rung-4 estimate consumer in bennett-conformance has no full-launch input and uses an infeasible target. Evidence: (1) the only available .tmp/rung-4/runs objects are reduced rung4-mini.bennett diagnostics (20261101T213213.441081Z and 20261101T221646.155856Z) with ISA/object/launch/sched/cert 0.8 headers, four lprocs and a 16-byte data image, not the actual N=2^20 launch; the estimator pins the published complete ref 0.9 library and no ref 0.8 expansion is published, so applying 0.9 costs to the legacy diagnostic would invent a binding; a full modern launch artifact remains required. (2) The named target in rung-4 DESIGN §6, superconducting-grid-illustrative.json, has data.capacity=16 and buffer.capacity=4; ISA §8.4/§11 require class capacity, and the required 2^28-wire interface fits neither class (nor their sum), so reporting a feasible exact cost under it would be false.

Proposed exact change to ladder/rung-4/DESIGN.md §6 and its pinned target entry: "Use the published ideal-all-to-all.json named target for the full N=2^20 resource forecast. Its logical data class is unbounded. Bind its exact target hash and report reference-construction costs under the unchanged complete launch object, resolved arguments and budget tuple. Retain the finite superconducting-grid-illustrative.json model as an explicit infeasibility diagnostic. Do not reduce the database, register width, program, oracle count or quantum domain to fit that small target."
Also: pass the resolved subject/arguments/budget to the estimator adapter and accept its bound object_hash, target_hash, invocation.budget, resources and exact_resources fields (or add explicit aliases) instead of relying on a zero-budget CLI default to infer pins.json. The specs fix bindings, not the adapter spelling.

Determining sentence: Rung 3 intentionally forces reversible main, `out/main`, a bennett.argv reply, i32 status, no other host requests and a console-only tape. This is a neutral finding for the mixed case described in F28; it does not establish a current runtime failure.

Requested change: Keep this exact hello-world whole-device test. Label its helpers/profile accordingly; a mixed rung has native main plus named device entries and boundary-specific service expectations. Do not require main/argv or forbid ordinary native I/O in the mixed host; device effect/replay expectations remain exact per run.

Document them as the whole-device entry profile; the future mixed helper selects named marked entries with its own boundary service expectations and does not require native main to be an ISA entry or put native I/O on the R tape.

Cheap now: Yes: helper/profile scope and additive design.

title: Keep comparison-link libc restrictions local to the materialised comparator (fat-object audit F26)
description:
Source: bennett-isa-spec/docs/notes/2026-11-02-4ht-audit/cross-repo-beads.md, F26 (audit: AUDIT.md row F26). Parent context: bennett-4ht (fat object far star; no early decision may lock it out). Future mechanics: design/publication or focused acceptance task, not permission to implement an unpublished interface, not a stop condition for current rungs.

Owner: `bennett-conformance`  
Type: `task`  
Priority: `P3`  
Labels: `fat-object`  
Parent context: `bennett-4ht`  
Audit severity: **neutral**

Source: [rung-1 gate.py:264–307][r1-comparison]; [rung-3 gate.py:188–225][r3-comparison]; [rung-4 gate.py:523–540][r4-comparison]; [rung-4 DESIGN §§3/10][r4-design]. See [AUDIT.md](AUDIT.md), row F26, and the [shared scope](../2026-11-02-rev2/fat-object-scope.md).

Determining sentence: Materialised closure comparisons forbid host libc and require fixed/pinned link inputs; rung 1's `_start` is a comparison harness. These constraints are correct for those comparisons. This is a neutral finding for the mixed case described in F26; it does not establish a current runtime failure.

Requested change: Scope these exact restrictions to the materialised comparison executable. Add a separate ordinary-native-host baseline and execution row for mixed mode, while keeping the existing closure comparison, classifiers and no-host-libc checks intact. Do not apply `-nostdlib`, no NEEDED, or the comparison input allowlist to the production native host.

Acceptance: Annotate rung-1/3/4 comparison helpers as device-closure comparators. Preserve existing pinned input, no-host-libc and fixed-address checks there, while the separate mixed host baseline/production executable may use ordinary host libc. A weaker comparator or host-libc-only baseline cannot satisfy the original rungs.

Cheap now: Yes: design wording; extra run when mixed ABI lands.

title: differential: replay rejects table/reference mismatch before the target is known; checker defers to unchecked
description: What: on controlled-action-09 as published in bennett-isa-spec (run without --target/--schedule), 15 table mutants (drop/dup/swap/flip/short/long/noncanonical/number/out_of_range/row_field/tuple_field) are rejected by checker-replay (E_REPLAY_MISMATCH/E_REPLAY_TABLE) and left unchecked by bennett-check ('target document is missing'). Neither accepts. The replay's reject relies on a legal realisation of the scheduled subject agreeing with its reference semantics on basis states; the comparison relation (§12.1) is realised-vs-table. Schema faults (row_field, tuple_field, number, noncanonical, short, long) are definitive regardless; the value mismatches assume that agreement. Evidence: checker-replay/witnesses/table-without-target. Decide whether the replay should report value mismatches without a target as unchecked.

title: checker: capability boundary seen by the differential (lproc, memory rows, H/Z/H and T/Tdg actions, adj call) and a 120 s timeout on arith.bij.addmod.w8.mfb
description: What: checker-replay replays these synthetic claims (hand-derived facts, checker-replay/checker_replay/synthetic.py) while bennett-check (e5bc3af) reports unchecked: lproc-depth-limit, lproc-recursive-sum, lproc-stack-monotonic, lproc-step-budget, oracle-alloc-zero-bumps, oracle-double-free, oracle-free-pinned, oracle-global-load, oracle-heap-limit, oracle-load-past-end, oracle-parmov, oracle-store-load-heap (evidence) and action-adj-call, action-hzh, action-ttdg (proof). Consistent with docs/checker.md's stated boundary; listed so the extension has ready witnesses. Separately the debug binary exceeded the harness's 120 s per-case timeout on the published bennett-arith/adders/objects/arith.bij.addmod.w8.mfb.bisa (and two of its object mutants) on a loaded host (load ~30); checker-replay finishes it (proof on both exhaustive claims, overall unchecked for out-of-scope items). Evidence: checker-replay/witnesses/lproc-recursive-sum, oracle-store-load-heap, action-hzh, timeout-addmod-w8.

title: checker: reports unchecked where a claim is definitively ill-formed (absent subject/program closure, oracle relation on an action)
description: What: for an object with no imports section, bennett-check (e5bc3af) reports unchecked ('subject region is not in the supplied object', 'expected program is not in the supplied object') where no linked library can supply the closure, and unchecked for expected "oracle" on an action subject (§12.1: the oracle relation compares to §5.2's oracle map and needs an oracle). checker-replay rejects all three (E_REPLAY_SUBJECT/E_REPLAY_EXPECTED). Not unsound (nothing accepted), but weaker than the spec allows. Counts in diff2: 49 + 49 + 3 mutants. Evidence: checker-replay/witnesses/unchecked-subject-closure-absent, unchecked-program-absent, unchecked-oracle-on-action.
